answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one operator across a thousand names does not multiply its capital: every name needs collateral, and detected coordination burns it. The sable broker may sell a gale of fable identities, but it cannot make their deposits free; the attacker pays upfront and risks losing the full bond.
